title: Quantum Machine Learning for Few-Shot Impersonation Detection in Digital Account Opening
summary: Identity impersonation fraud may emerge only after digital account opening, requiring an early post-onboarding approach based on behavioral and transactional signals observed shortly after activation. Confirmed cases remain rare, creating extreme class imbalance and material operational risk for digital banks. We evaluate quantum machine learning (QML) against classical one-class methods in this setting using a real 2025 cohort of 3,419 digital account openings from Banco de Creditos e Inversiones (BCI), Chile, including 8 confirmed impersonation-fraud cases (0.23% prevalence).
